questions.q: What is the key difference between training loss and held-out (validation) loss?
options: There is no difference -- they are always identical for any trained model
Training loss measures fit to the exact batches optimized on, while held-out loss measures generalization to data the model never trained on
Held-out loss is always lower than training loss
Training loss can only be computed after training is fully complete
questions.explain: Training loss reflects fit to the training batches themselves, while held-out loss, computed on unseen validation data, reflects how well that fit generalizes -- the two can diverge, which signals overfitting.

questions.q: What does it mean when training loss keeps falling while held-out loss plateaus or rises?
options: The model is training perfectly with no issues
This is the signature of overfitting -- the model is increasingly fitting idiosyncrasies of the training data rather than learning generalizable patterns
The held-out set was corrupted and should be discarded
The learning rate is too low and should be increased
questions.explain: A widening gap between falling training loss and plateauing or rising held-out loss is the classic signature of overfitting to the training distribution.

questions.q: How is perplexity computed from loss, and what does it represent intuitively?
options: Perplexity is the square root of the loss, representing training speed

Perplexity is exp(loss), representing the model's average effective branching factor over the next token -- e.g., a perplexity of 20 means uncertainty comparable to choosing uniformly among 20 options
Perplexity is the loss divided by the number of parameters
Perplexity has no mathematical relationship to loss
questions.explain: Perplexity is the exponential of the cross-entropy loss, giving an intuitive 'effective branching factor' interpretation of the model's next-token uncertainty.

questions.q: Why can a model have excellent perplexity on held-out web text while still being mediocre at following instructions?
options: Perplexity and instruction-following are mathematically identical, so this scenario is impossible
Perplexity measures next-token prediction on a specific data distribution, while instruction-following is a different, narrower distribution that perplexity does not directly measure
Instruction-following can only be measured by perplexity on code data
A model's perplexity score always determines its instruction-following ability exactly
questions.explain: Perplexity reflects performance on whatever distribution the held-out set is drawn from; instruction-following is a distinct downstream capability that low perplexity on general text does not guarantee.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe held-out loss and perplexity as 'necessary but not sufficient' for evaluating an LLM?
options: Because they are completely useless and should never be measured
Because they measure next-token prediction quality well, but don't directly measure instruction-following, reasoning accuracy, or harmful-output avoidance, which require other evaluation methods
Because they can only be computed on models smaller than 1 billion parameters
Because perplexity is identical to human evaluation scores
questions.explain: Held-out loss and perplexity are a cheap, necessary first check on next-token prediction, but they structurally cannot measure instruction-following, reasoning, or safety -- which is why benchmarks and human evaluation are also needed.
